description: The New York Tunnels system is the classic water-supply design benchmark from Schaake and Lai (1969), and the Modified New York Tunnels version comes from Bi and Dandy (2014); Graeme Dandy contributed both to the Water Distribution System Research Database (entries 26 and 38). Each entry offers a system description PDF and an EPANET zip, and DataCite holds DOIs for both. According to the summary spreadsheet, each has 21 pipes, one reservoir and 19 nodes in a looped layout, with no pumps or tanks; the demand is listed as 1,305 million gallons per day for the original and 961.58 for the modified network, and the modified network is marked as having water-quality information. Coverage is the New York City tunnel problem, a design case, not a calibrated model. The files are free; no licence is stated on the pages, only a copyright notice. Only the index page, the entry pages, the summary spreadsheet and DataCite metadata were read; no network file was downloaded or run. The networks are used to test tunnel-duplication and pipe-sizing optimisation, evolutionary algorithms and hydraulic solvers. Related records: EPANET, the database record, and the Extended Hanoi and other benchmark networks of the same contributor.
